label: Dentist visit

what_happens.title: What happens at the dentist
goals: A dentist is a doctor who keeps teeth strong and clean
The visit follows the same steps every time: door, waiting room, big chair, counting teeth, a sticker
Nothing is a surprise: the dentist shows and tells before doing
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the steps in order and ask your child to say what comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the dentist
goals: The front desk helper, the dental assistant and the dentist each have one job
They wear masks and gloves to keep everyone clean, and smile behind the mask
The grown-up stays close the whole time
who_is_there.parentSkill: Talk about the helpers by their job, so new faces feel like part of the plan.

what_i_do.title: What I do in the big chair
goals: The child's jobs: sit back, open wide, keep hands on the tummy
Raising a hand means 'I need a break', and the dentist stops
The child can count teeth with the dentist
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise 'open wide' and the stop signal with a mirror and a toothbrush.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared
goals: Feeling scared is okay and many children feel it
Some things may tickle, press or pinch a little, and that feeling ends
Calm-down tools: slow breaths, holding a hand or a foot, sunglasses for the bright light
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling without fixing it: 'You feel worried. I'm right here.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the dentist
goals: Play dentist at home with a toothbrush and a toy
Go through every step once more, ending with the sticker
Celebrate the child's bravery and the plan for afterwards
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child be the dentist first, then switch roles.

steps: Walk in through the clinic door and say hello at the front desk
Wait in the waiting room until the child's name is called
Sit in the big chair that moves up and leans back
Put on sunglasses for the bright light above
Open wide while the dentist counts and checks each tooth with a tiny mirror
Teeth are cleaned with a buzzy brush and rinsed with water
Pick a sticker and go home
sensory: a bright lamp over the chair
a buzzing sound from the little brush
a minty or fruity taste of toothpaste
cool water and a slurpy straw that sucks it up
a chair that hums as it moves
gloves and masks on the helpers
honestyNotes: May feel a little pinch, press or tickle. Never promise 'no pain'. Say the feeling is short and the dentist stops when the child raises a hand.

fallbackAnswer: Most of the visit feels like tickles and presses.
Sometimes a tooth feels a little pinch, and then it stops.
If you need a break, raise your hand and the dentist will wait.
Yes, [[GROWNUP]] can stay in the room with you.
You can look at [[GROWNUP]] or hold a hand or a foot the whole time.
The tiny mirror helps the dentist see the back of your teeth.
The buzzy brush cleans them, and the little straw slurps up the water.
You can ask the dentist to show you each tool first.

questionButtons.text: Why is the light so bright?
fallbackAnswer: The bright light helps the dentist see inside your mouth.
You can wear sunglasses, and you can close your eyes too.
A dentist is a doctor whose job is keeping teeth healthy.
The dentist will say hello and tell you each step before doing it.
When your teeth are counted and clean, the chair goes back down.
Then you pick a sticker, and you go home with [[GROWNUP]].

techniques.label: Holding a hand or a foot
techniques.how: Sit or stand where your child can reach you and hold a hand or a foot during the check.

techniques.label: Counting teeth together
techniques.how: Ask the dentist to count teeth out loud and count along in your head or with your fingers.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during each part of the check; many parts are done before ten.

techniques.label: Wearing sunglasses
techniques.how: Bring your child's own sunglasses or ask for a pair to soften the bright lamp.

techniques.label: Choosing a sticker after
techniques.how: Talk about the sticker or a small treat at the end, so there is something to look forward to.

techniques.label: The hand-up stop signal
techniques.how: Agree with the dentist that a raised hand means 'please wait', and practise it at home.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out through the mouth like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Let your child bring a favourite toy to hold in the waiting room and in the chair.

pain: It might feel like a tickle or a little pinch, and then it's over.
You can raise your hand any time and the dentist will wait.
separation: I'll be right here in the room. You can look at me the whole time.
You can hold my hand or I can hold your foot.
unknown: First the big chair, then counting teeth, then a sticker.
The dentist will show you each tool before using it.
strangers: The dentist's job is to keep teeth healthy. Let's say hello together.
They wear masks to keep things clean. There's a smile under there.
sensory: The light is bright so the dentist can see. Sunglasses help.
The little brush buzzes. It sounds louder than it feels.
safety: The dentist does this every day and knows how to keep you safe.
If something feels wrong, raise your hand and they stop.
body: The dentist only looks at your mouth and teeth.
You decide when you need a break.
love: I'm proud of you for trying, whatever happens.
social: Other children come to the dentist too. Everyone waits their turn.
You can wave hello to the other kids in the waiting room.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will visit the dentist.
A dentist is a doctor who helps teeth stay strong and clean.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] walk through the clinic door.
Then they say hello at the front desk.
Next, they sit in the waiting room until [[CHILD]]'s name is called.
Then [[CHILD]] climbs into a big chair that hums and leans back.
A bright light shines above, so the dentist can see.
The dentist shows a tiny mirror and counts every tooth.
After that, a buzzy brush cleans the teeth.
At the end, [[CHILD]] picks a sticker.
At the front desk, a helper smiles and says hello to [[CHILD]].
In the room there is a dental assistant who hands the dentist the tools.
Then the dentist comes in and says a friendly name.
Each helper has one job: keeping teeth healthy.
The helpers wear masks and gloves to keep everything clean.
Under each mask there is a smile.
[[GROWNUP]] stays right there in the room, close to [[CHILD]].
[[CHILD]] can look at [[GROWNUP]] any time.
Everyone in the room is on [[CHILD]]'s team.
In the big chair, [[CHILD]] has three jobs.
Sit back like a sleepy cat.
Open wide like a big yawn.
Keep both hands resting on the tummy.
The dentist counts each tooth, and [[CHILD]] can count along in a quiet head voice.
Sometimes a mouth gets tired of being open.
Then [[CHILD]] can raise one hand high.
A raised hand means please wait, and the dentist will stop for a break.
After a little rest, the counting goes on.
[[CHILD]] is the boss of the stop signal.
Lots of children feel a little scared at the dentist, and that is okay.
Some things tickle, some things press, and sometimes a tooth feels a small pinch.
That feeling is short, and then it stops.
[[CHILD]] can smell a flower and blow out a candle, slow and soft.
If the bright light feels too much, [[CHILD]] can wear sunglasses.
If the buzzy sound feels loud, [[CHILD]] can count teeth with the dentist.
[[GROWNUP]] can hold a hand or a foot the whole time.
Brave does not mean not scared.
Brave means trying with a helper close by.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play dentist at home.
A favourite toy sits in the big chair.
[[CHILD]] says, open wide, and counts the toy's teeth with a toothbrush.
Then they switch, and [[GROWNUP]] counts [[CHILD]]'s teeth.
Remember the stop signal: one hand up.
Let's say the steps one more time.
First the door, then the waiting room, then the big chair.
Next, open wide and count teeth.
After that, pick a sticker.
[[CHILD]] knows every step now, and [[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] for practising.
My name is [[CHILD]], and soon I will go to the dentist.
A dentist is a doctor who checks and cleans teeth.
First, I walk through the clinic door with [[GROWNUP]].
Then we say hello at the front desk and sit in the waiting room.
I can bring a toy to hold while I wait.
Next, a helper says my name, and I go to a room with a big chair.
The chair moves up and leans back.
There is a bright light above the chair.
The dentist counts my teeth and cleans them with a small brush that buzzes.
When it is done, I can pick a sticker.
I can try to sit still.
At the dentist there are a few people who help.
A helper at the front desk writes down my name.
A dental assistant gets the tools ready.
The dentist checks my teeth.
I can say hello or wave.
The helpers wear masks and gloves.
Masks and gloves keep everything clean.
[[GROWNUP]] stays in the room with me.
I can look at [[GROWNUP]] when I want to.
Many children go to the dentist two times a year.
The dentist knows how to help children.
When I sit in the big chair, I lean back.
The dentist will ask me to open my mouth wide.
The dentist uses a tiny mirror to look at each tooth.
I can try to keep my hands on my tummy.
The dentist may count my teeth out loud.
Sometimes my mouth gets tired.
If I need a break, I can raise my hand.
When I raise my hand, the dentist will stop and wait.
Then the dentist will start again when I am ready.
Raising my hand is a safe way to say stop.
Some children feel worried at the dentist.
Feeling worried is okay.
Some things may tickle or press, and sometimes I may feel a small pinch.
The feeling is short.
I can breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly.
The light is bright, and the brush makes a buzzing sound.
I can wear sunglasses to make the light softer.
[[GROWNUP]] can hold my hand or my foot.
The visit has an end.
After the visit, I go home.
At home, I can practise going to the dentist.
I sit on a chair and lean back.
[[GROWNUP]] counts my teeth with a toothbrush.
I can practise opening wide and raising my hand to say stop.
Then I can count the teeth of my toy.
Here are the steps.
First, the waiting room.
Then, the big chair and the bright light.
Next, the dentist counts and cleans my teeth.
After that, I pick a sticker.
I practised all the steps, and that was a good job.
